newsitem.title: USA: COMEX copper ends down, shrugs off Portugal strike.
newsitem.headline: COMEX copper ends down, shrugs off Portugal strike.

text.p: COMEX copper ended weaker after the market failed to make any significant headway on the upside in early dealings amid further hikes in LME stocks.
The market also shrugged off news of an indefinite strike at the 100,000 tonnes a year Neves Corvo copper mine in Portugal.
LME stocks rose 1,250 tonnes to 131,100 tonnes Monday.

Bette Raptopoulos of Prudential Securities said the poor close in copper was also partly linked to the rout in gold and other precious metals as some funds may have sold copper to compensate for losses elsewhere, or sold the metal as part of their portfolio basket of metals.
September COMEX copper settled 1.70 cents weaker at 109.55 cents a lb, traded 111.80 to 109.30 cents. Spot July went out 1.90 cents lower at 111.55 cents.
The CFTC commitment of traders report for week ended July 1, released Monday due to Independence Day holiday Friday, showed that speculators were still long and commercials short.
Speculators held 14,788 long positions and 2,771 short positions, while the trade was short to the tune of 32,521 positions and long 13,214 positions.
Brokers were paying particular attention to the upcoming July Third Wednesday pricing on LME. The Third Wednesday is July 16, but the pricing will be done the prior Monday, July 14.
The nearby tightness runs from that date through month end.
The LME cash to three months backwardation was stable at $132/$142.
